claim_verbatim: "The P-CSEM and base models were evaluated against a different dataset of cholecystectomy tools from the EndoVis 2019 [25] challenge. This evaluation was performed in order to observe the generalizability of the trained model on data from a different source." (Discussion)
setting: EndoVis 2019 challenge data (reference [25] is the HeiChole benchmark), restricted to classes shared with Cholec80
contrast: Yes, implicit: "not able to achieve comparable mAP results as in the Chole80 dataset" (59.52% external vs 93.14% internal)
D2_quote: "This evaluation was performed in order to observe the generalizability of the trained model on data from a different source." (Discussion). Cholec80: "recorded at the University Hospital of Strasbourg" (3.1); no centre or duplicate check given for the external set.
D5_quote: "the mean of the average precision (mAP) of each of the tools was determined across the testing set." (2.6 Evaluation Criteria)
D7_quote: "Although these models were not able to achieve comparable mAP results as in the Chole80 dataset," (Discussion); internal mAP 93.14 in Table 2
D8_quote: "This evaluation was performed in order to observe the generalizability of the trained model" (Discussion)
supportable_claim: The Cholec80-trained classifier reached 59.52% mAP (base model 58.57%) on an EndoVis 2019/HeiChole subset, versus 93.14% internally. The size of that subset, the frames used, how it was annotated and whether it is disjoint from Cholec80 are not reported, so the result cannot be checked or interpreted as generalisation.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The abstract and conclusions make no external claim (the abstract says 'trained and tested on ... Cholec80'). Rule added: if the abstract and conclusion contain no external claim, rate the first external claim in the body. External results appear only in the Discussion text, not in any table. Classes not in Cholec80 were removed, with an explanation, so D4 is r (not n). Rated r for D3: the data availability statement covers Cholec80 only, with no code and no statement on the external data. Reference [25] is cited as EndoVis 2019 but the reference list gives the HeiChole benchmark.

claim_verbatim: "Our findings indicate that domain-specific pretraining with EndoViT yields notable advantages in complex downstream tasks. In the case of action triplet recognition, our approach outperforms ImageNet pretraining. In semantic segmentation, we surpass the state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance." (Abstract, Results)
behaviour: Semantic segmentation (mIoU), action triplet recognition (mAP), phase recognition (accuracy) after fine-tuning
setting: Cholec80 and its derivatives CholecT45 and CholecSeg8k (single source, which is also part of the Endo700k pretraining corpus)
contrast: None between settings. The comparison is EndoViT versus ImageNet pretraining and prior SOTA.
D1_quote: Table 1: "Cholec80 [26] | Laparoscopic cholecystectomy | 80 | 184,498" listed in Endo700k; "The downstream evaluation experiments are conducted on the Cholec80 dataset [26] and its subvariants" (Methods)
D2_quote: "To eliminate any potential data leakage, we exclude any images that appear in their validation or test sets from the pretraining dataset." (Methods)
D3_quote: "We release both our code and pretrained models to facilitate further research in this direction:" (Abstract); splits only by citation: "We replicate the evaluation setup of [24]."
D5_quote: "The reported metric is mean Intersection over Union (IoU)." (segmentation); "The reported metric is mean Average Precision (mAP) proposed by the authors of the CholecT45 dataset" (triplet)
supportable_claim: After fine-tuning on Cholec80-family training splits, EndoViT matched or exceeded ImageNet-pretrained ViT on Cholec80-family test splits from one source (Strasbourg), whose training images are also in the pretraining corpus. This is a same-source benchmark result, not external validation.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The abstract makes no claim of other-centre or other-source performance. I rated its main downstream-performance claim. Rule added: when the claim makes no internal-versus-external contrast, D7 and D8 are x, as the protocol says. Fine-tuning on the downstream data is noted here instead ('the EndoViT encoder can be finetuned'). The leakage control is at image level for each named dataset. It is unclear whether Cholec80 frames from CholecSeg8k test videos were removed, so D2 is p. The GitHub repository could not be accessed (not on the fetch allowlist), so any split files in it were not checked. PMC copy PMC11178556 was blocked by a captcha. S03 is the arXiv v1 of this same work.

claim_verbatim: "Through ablations, we demonstrate that domain-specific pretraining is particularly beneficial for more complex downstream tasks, such as Action Triplet Detection, and less effective and even unnecessary for simpler tasks, such as Surgical Phase Recognition." (Abstract)
behaviour: Action triplet detection (mAP) and surgical phase recognition (accuracy) after fine-tuning
setting: Cholec80 and CholecT45 (single source, which is also part of the Endo700k pretraining corpus)
contrast: None between settings. The comparison is EndoViT versus ImageNet pretraining.
D1_quote: "First, testing only on one fold allows us to have CholecT45 images in the pretraining." (Action Triplet Detection); "Outside the previously mentioned exceptions, we use all of the images from the nine datasets."
D2_quote: "To eliminate any potential data leakage, we do not include any images that appear in their validation or test sets." (Methods)
D3_quote: "Although the authors of CholecT45 propose a cross-validation setup, we decided to test only on fold 5." (split by reference); "We will release both our code and pretrained models upon acceptance" (Abstract)
D5_quote: "domain-specific pretraining is particularly beneficial for more complex downstream tasks, such as Action Triplet Detection" (Abstract); metric is mAP with no localisation (per retrieved Methods text; verbatim metric sentence not captured)
supportable_claim: After fine-tuning, Endo700k pretraining improved CholecT45 fold-5 triplet recognition mAP over ImageNet, with negligible differences for Cholec80 phase recognition, on same-source data that is partly in the pretraining corpus. No external-source evidence.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The full text came through ar5iv because arxiv.org PDF retrieval returned only the abstract. The ar5iv page carries the v1 title, but the version was not confirmed. The D5 metric description comes from a web text extraction summary, not a verbatim sentence. Verify it. Rule added for D5: when 'detection' in the claim refers to frame-level presence recognition with no localisation metric, rate p (not n) and note it. D7 and D8 are x because no settings are compared. Fine-tuning on downstream data was used. The code was promised upon acceptance and not provided in this version. This is the preprint of S02, so S02 and S03 are not independent.

claim_verbatim: We also evaluated the generalizability of our method to similar tasks using two public datasets. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) self-supervised representation learning methods in various surgical image segmentation tasks.
behaviour: Instrument type/part segmentation (EndoVisSub2017-RIS) and 8-class tissue/instrument segmentation (CholecSeg8k); mIoU/mDice
unit: Dataset (public datasets distinct from the in-house IVIS development data)
setting: EndoVisSub2017-RIS (porcine, da Vinci Xi; test sequences 9-10) and CholecSeg8k (Cholec80 subset from CAMMA; 1,040 test images), each after fine-tuning on its own training split
contrast: None stated; comparison is against other pretraining/segmentation methods, not internal vs external
D1_quote: "use 2, 400 images of eight sequences (#1-8) for fine-tuning and 600 images of two sequences (#9-10) for testing" (Sec. V-A Datasets and Settings)
D2_quote: "CholecSeg8k dataset is a subset of the endoscopic images of Cholec80 provided by CAMMA" (Sec. V-A)
D3_quote: "The inference code and the pretrained model of our SurgNet, as well as the End User License Agreement (EULA) for applying our IVIS surgical image dataset can be found at: https://github.com/HanHuCAS/SurgNet" (Footnote 1, p. 1515)
D4_quote: "perform 8-class segmentation on CholecSeg8k using 7, 040 images for fine-tuning and 1, 040 images for testing" (Sec. V-A)
D5_quote: "use mIoU and mDice for multi-class segmentation tasks" (Sec. V-A)
D6_quote: "The dataset is annotated with 7 types of surgical instruments" (Sec. V-A, EndoVisSub2017-RIS)
D7_quote: "Both our method and UM-MAE achieve nearly 80% mIoU and 90% Dice" (Sec. V-C, Table III, IVIS-E instrument segmentation)
D8_quote: "we need to fine-tune the network using the labeled data in individual downstream tasks" (Sec. III-D)
supportable_claim: After fine-tuning on each public dataset's own training split, SurgNet-pretrained models gave higher mIoU than the compared methods on EndoVisSub2017-RIS test sequences 9-10 (0.63 type / 0.81 part) and on a CholecSeg8k test split of unreported split unit (0.71). This supports transfer of the pretraining after re-training on the target data, not performance of a fixed model on unseen external data; several baselines were copied from other papers.
notes: Rule R1: claim covers EndoVisSub2017-RIS and CholecSeg8k. D1: EndoVis split is sequence-level; CholecSeg8k split follows [77] with unit not stated; IVIS (human, PLA hospital) vs porcine EndoVis is disjoint by species but not stated. D2: external sources differ from IVIS, but no duplicate control between external fine-tuning and test splits, which both enter development once fine-tuned. D3: only inference code + pretrained backbone; no fine-tuning code or fine-tuned weights; EndoVis split given, CholecSeg8k split by reference. D4: totals only, no per-class counts (Tables IV-V give means). D7 (R2): IVIS-E internal mIoU reported, but on a different class set. D8: no zero-shot external estimate; model fine-tuned on every external dataset. EndoVis18 comparison (0.845 mIoU) is a secondary claim, not rated. Decision rules applied: (R1) a single claim sentence naming several external datasets/scenarios is rated across all of them and the lower rating is recorded; (R2) D7 is rated when the report presents development and external results for the model or interprets a cross-setting difference, x otherwise; (R3) D8 is rated even when D7 is x if the report documents changing the model or operating threshold on the external data; if a zero-shot estimate is clearly separated but the claim rests on the adapted/tuned estimate, D8 = p; (R4) data 'available on request' with no code or manifest = D3 a.

Specifically, there are improvements of 1.6 percentage points in balanced accuracy for the foreground, 1.7 points in intersection over union (IoU), and 1.7 points in mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC)." (Abstract)
behaviour: Binary robotic tool segmentation; IoU, DSC, balanced accuracy
setting: Stated: DVR (dVRK ex vivo) test videos, Internet videos (U.S. National Library of Medicine) and EndoVis 17. Results are reported only for the DVR test set.
contrast: None between settings. The comparison is EUGNet versus U-Net.
D1_quote: "The training set contains four ex vivo 45 s videos." "The testing set consists of four 15 s and two 60 s videos." (Datasets); results "on the DVR testing dataset" (Conclusions)
D3_quote: "The data presented in this study are available at" [Roboflow URL] (Data Availability); Internet videos: "(video links are available upon request)"
D4_quote: "This means that we have a total of (60 + 15) × 25 = 1875 frames (images)." (DVR dataset)
D5_quote: "1.7 points in intersection over union (IoU), and 1.7 points in mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC)." (Abstract)
D6_quote: "The ground truth masks are automatically generated using joint encoder information and forward kinematics. Hand-eye calibration errors are manually corrected." (DVR dataset)
supportable_claim: On held-out ex vivo dVRK videos from the same source as training, EUGNet improved IoU and DSC over U-Net by about 1.7 points. No quantitative results are reported for the Internet (NLM) or other-source videos.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The review's external classification probably rests on the Internet/NLM videos, but no results or reference standard are reported for them. Ratings are therefore given for the evaluation actually reported (the DVR test set), whose split is at video level within one source: D1 is n because the split is at a lower unit than the dataset claim. The frame count is inconsistent: 4×15 s + 2×60 s = 180 s ≈ 4500 frames at 25 fps, not 1875. The EndoVis 17 split description is internally inconsistent (600 images versus 10×300 frames). There is no code statement.

claim_verbatim: "Focusing on the application of PAWSS to surgical scenes, we evaluate on MICCAI 2015 challenge instrument tracking challenge and in vivo datasets, showing that our approach performs the best among all submitted methods and also has promising performance on in vivo surgical instrument tracking." (Abstract)
behaviour: Surgical instrument tracking; average distance error in pixels (official challenge), percentage of frames within threshold
unit: dataset (challenge test sets and in vivo sequences)
setting: MICCAI 2015 EndoVis instrument tracking (ex vivo robotic and in vivo conventional) test sets, scored by the organisers, and other in vivo sequences (Fig. 18)
contrast: None between settings. The comparison is against other challenge submissions.
D1_quote: "Test data is composed of 15 additional seconds video from each of the training sequence" "and two additional new 60 s video sequences." (Datasets)
D2_quote: "It does not require prior information about the target or any offline training to achieve robust and realtime performance." (Conclusion); in vivo: "We also test on some other in vivo sequences and show the result in Fig. 18."
D3_quote: "Our algorithm is publicly available online" (github.com/surgical-vision/PAWSS); "The dataset has not released ground truth for test data."
D4_quote: "test data is made up of 15 additional seconds videos for each sequence" "two new 60 s videos." (Datasets); no frame counts for the test sets or the Fig. 18 sequences
D5_quote: "outperforms all the other methods with the lowest average distance error 29.66 pixels." (Results, robotic)
D6_quote: "We submitted our proposed method to the challenge, and obtained the performance comparison from the official report." / "the quality of the annotation is not consistent through the whole sequence."
supportable_claim: On the MICCAI 2015 EndoVis tracking test sets (ex vivo robotic and in vivo conventional), scored by the organisers against ground truth that is not released, PAWSS had the lowest average distance error among submitted methods (29.66 and 96.78 px). Performance on the other in vivo sequences is shown only qualitatively.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. PAWSS is an online tracker with no offline training, so the 'development data' is only the parameter selection on OTB and VOT. The test set includes 15-s continuations of the training sequences; for a tracker with no offline training this is not leakage, but it does break disjointness at the video unit, so D1 is p. The 'same parameter setting through all experiments' statement would support D8, but D8 is x by protocol because no settings are compared. The in vivo 'promising performance' (Fig. 18) has no reference standard or metric. This is the main reason claim_supported is no.

claim_verbatim: "We conducted extensive experiments on different datasets to validate these findings. The results showed that the end-to-end network successfully improved the state-of-the-art for both tasks while reducing the complexity during their deployment." (Abstract)
behaviour: Depth estimation (SSIM) and tool segmentation (Jaccard, Dice). The external test covers depth SSIM only.
setting: Second dataset, ref [28] (Mountney, Stoyanov and Yang 2010; Hamlyn in vivo data; name garbled in the extracted text), tested with the model trained on DB80 (ref [27], Ye et al. 2017)
contrast: Yes: DB80 (Table II) vs second dataset (Table III) SSIM; "confirming that the SDSNET generalizes well across different datasets" (Generalization)
D5_quote: "For the depth estimation branch, similar to [29], we used the SSIM index to evaluate the unsupervised depth estimation." (Experimental Setup)
D7_quote: "we used the SSIM index to evaluate the unsupervised depth estimation." (Experimental Setup); internal DB80 SSIM in Table II; "Table III represents the results of SDSNET and Monodepth2 in this experiment using the SSIM index." (Generalization)
D8_quote: "an additional experiment used the model trained on the DB80 dataset but tested directly on the D ?>A dataset, without retraining the whole network." (Generalization)

Depth accuracy against ground truth and segmentation were not evaluated externally, and the size of the external test set is not reported.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The second dataset's name is garbled in the core.ac.uk text extraction ('D ?>A'). It is identified only through reference [28]. SSIM measures photometric reconstruction, not depth error, so D5 is n for the depth claim. Segmentation was evaluated only on 400 manually labelled images from an unspecified dataset. Both cited datasets come from the Hamlyn Centre group, but the paper does not state the centres, so D2 is r. 'without retraining the whole network' leaves partial retraining open, so D8 is p. There is no code or data statement.

fulltext_url: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.17904v1 (also https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.17904v2; accepted-manuscript preprint of the LNCS chapter)
claim_verbatim: "However, extending this data with more heterogeneous surgical data further increases performance by an additional 5.0%, 5.2%, and 2.5%, suggesting that increasing diversity within SSL data is beneficial for model performance." (Abstract)
behaviour: Semantic segmentation after SSL pretraining and fine-tuning; Dice
unit: patient (test patients excluded from pretraining); claim spans three downstream datasets
setting: CholecSeg8k (Cholec80-derived), RAMIE (UMCU) and RARP (AvL, single centre). All three sources also contribute to the SurgeNet pretraining corpus.
contrast: None between settings. The comparison is pretraining data compositions versus ImageNet.
D1_quote: "It should be noted that all videos of patients included in the test set are excluded from SurgeNet." (2.1); "Among these, 6,800 (84%) were used for training and 1,280 (16%) were selected for testing." (2.2)
D2_quote: "For the CholecSeg8k dataset, all patients present in the downstream training set are also included in the SurgeNet-pertaining dataset." "In the case of the RAMIE downstream dataset, 22 of the 50 patient videos are also included in the SurgeNet-pertaining dataset"
D3_quote: "The code and pretrained model weights are made publicly available at https://github.com/TimJaspers0801/SurgeNet."
D4_quote: "Among these, 6,800 (84%) were used for training and 1,280 (16%) were selected for testing." (2.2); "For the test set, one frame from 30 different patient videos was annotated."
D5_quote: "Segmentation results (Dice scores) on the three downstream datasets from the fivefold cross-validation." (Fig. 1 caption)
D6_quote: "For the test set, one frame from 30 different patient videos was annotated." "while the expert surgeon solely completed test annotations" (2.2, RARP)

Whether the reported Dice comes from the held-out test sets or the cross-validation is ambiguous, and no evaluation on a centre absent from development is reported.
notes: Quotations were extracted from the web text from the URL given and must be checked against the PDF before consensus. The paper makes no explicit external claim; I rated the abstract's main claim. The unit was taken as patient because the only disjointness the report gives is patient-level exclusion of test videos from pretraining. The downstream train/test split level is not stated for CholecSeg8k, so D1 is p. The Fig. 1 caption reports Dice 'from the fivefold cross-validation', so it is unclear whether these are test-set results. Class counts are inconsistent: CholecSeg8k is said to have 13 classes with 4 removed, but Table 2 lists 8. The RAMIE centre is only inferred (Table 1 'RAMIE-UMCU'). Several quotes were truncated by the tool; re-check them against the LNCS version.

claim_verbatim: AI has potential to detect unsafe dissection and prevent BDIs through real-time intraoperative decision-support.
behaviour: Go/No-Go zone segmentation (GoNoGoNet) used to flag unsafe dissection; proportion of tool-tissue interactions outside the predicted Go zone and zone of the injurious act
setting: 11 retrospectively collected LC videos with bile duct injury (collaborator network and open-access sources) and 11 control videos from a 333-video bank, none used in training
contrast: BDI vs control videos; no internal vs external contrast
D1_quote: "None of the videos from either group had been used in the training of the model previously." (Methods, Dataset)
D2_quote: "LC videos with documented BDIs were procured from the authors’ network of collaborators as well as from open access sources." (Methods, Dataset)
D4_quote: "A total of 126:45 min of tool-tissue interactions (BDI group = 70:01 min; Control group = 56:44 min) were analyzed" (Results)
D5_quote: "GoNoGoNet detected 33.6% more total tissue interactions as being in the No-Go/in-between zones in the BDI group compared to the Control group." (Results)
D6_quote: "all tool-tissue interactions were compared to AI-annotated Go and No-Go zones on an initial reference frame within the same minute of each video." (Methods, Dataset)
D8_quote: "When the probability threshold of the algorithm for the Go zone was modulated, there were significantly less BDI interactions that occurred in the Go zone." (Results)
supportable_claim: In 22 retrospectively selected LC videos (11 with BDI, 11 expert-selected safe controls), a larger proportion of tool-tissue interactions lay outside GoNoGoNet's predicted Go zone in BDI videos (assessed against one AI reference frame per minute); at the default argmax rule 6/11 injurious acts lay inside the predicted Go zone. Detection of unsafe dissection (sensitivity/specificity) and prevention of BDI were not measured.
notes: D1 m on an explicit video-level non-use statement (no identifiers). D2: development set came from 136 institutions; BDI videos from collaborators/open access with no duplicate or source control. D4: interaction counts and sharp/blunt denominators not reported, only minutes; injurious acts n=11 given. D5: group-level proportion is a proxy, not a detection metric; prevention not assessed. D6: who labelled interactions not stated; AI zones taken from one reference frame per minute, not the frame of each interaction. D7 x (R2): no internal performance reported or compared. D8 (R3): default-threshold result is reported separately (4 No-Go, 6 Go, 1 in-between), but the abstract figure (2 Go, 18%) uses the threshold raised on these same external videos. The abstract reports only the tuned-threshold split of injurious acts (4 No-Go, 2 Go, 5 in-between at 80%), not the default-rule split. Decision rules applied: (R1) a single claim sentence naming several external datasets/scenarios is rated across all of them and the lower rating is recorded; (R2) D7 is rated when the report presents development and external results for the model or interprets a cross-setting difference, x otherwise; (R3) D8 is rated even when D7 is x if the report documents changing the model or operating threshold on the external data; if a zero-shot estimate is clearly separated but the claim rests on the adapted/tuned estimate, D8 = p; (R4) data 'available on request' with no code or manifest = D3 a.

claim_verbatim: AI can be used to identify safe and dangerous zones of dissection within the surgical field, with high specificity/PPV for Go zones and high sensitivity/NPV for No-Go zones.
behaviour: Go/No-Go zone semantic segmentation; Dice/IoU and pixel accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV against expert consensus
setting: 47 frames from 25 prospectively collected LC videos (7 institutions, 9 surgeons), annotated by 6 SAGES experts not involved in training
contrast: None in the claim; Discussion states replication of prior (development) results
D1_quote: "There were no duplicate videos and none were previously used in the original training dataset." (Results)
D2_quote: "Videos were obtained from 5 countries (Canada, USA, France, Bolivia and Thailand), 9 surgeons and 7 institutions." (Results)
D4_quote: "A total of 47 frames were extracted for validation." (Results)
D5_quote: "Identification of Go and No-Go zones by GoNoGoNet was compared to expert-derived consensus using mean F1 Dice Score, and pixel accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV)." (Abstract, Methods)
D6_quote: "A total of 47 frames from 25 LC videos, procured from 3 countries and 9 surgeons, were annotated simultaneously by an expert panel of 6 surgeons and GoNoGoNet." (Abstract, Results)
D7_quote: "Nevertheless, algorithmic performance seemed to replicate prior preliminary results [6]." (Discussion)
D8_quote: "A Convolutional DNN was previously trained to perform semantic segmentation (i.e. delineate the boundary) of the Go and No-Go zones of dissection during videos of LC [6]." (Methods, AI model)
supportable_claim: On 47 frames from 25 new LC videos from 7 institutions (overlap of institutions with the 136 development institutions not reported), the previously trained GoNoGoNet reached mean Dice 0.58 (Go) and 0.80 (No-Go) against a >50% six-expert consensus, with Go-zone PPV 0.70 and No-Go sensitivity 0.80; results vary with the consensus definition and cannot be replayed.
notes: D1 m on an explicit video-level statement. D2: 'no duplicate videos' is asserted without method; institutions not stated to be absent from development. D3: supplement is an annotation guide only; no code, data or manifest. D7 (R2): Discussion interprets external results as replicating development results, but internal metrics are only cited [6], not reported. D8: fixed model implied, not stated; operating rule (binary output) not specified. Abstract says 3 countries, Results 5 countries. The >50% consensus definition was highlighted after showing it gave the highest scores. Claim generalises beyond the sampled frames ('within the surgical field'); 'high' PPV for Go zone is 0.70 +/- 0.21. Decision rules applied: (R1) a single claim sentence naming several external datasets/scenarios is rated across all of them and the lower rating is recorded; (R2) D7 is rated when the report presents development and external results for the model or interprets a cross-setting difference, x otherwise; (R3) D8 is rated even when D7 is x if the report documents changing the model or operating threshold on the external data; if a zero-shot estimate is clearly separated but the claim rests on the adapted/tuned estimate, D8 = p; (R4) data 'available on request' with no code or manifest = D3 a.

fulltext_url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.07330v1.pdf (arXiv v1 preprint; also read via https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2309.07330)
claim_verbatim: For CVS criteria, we achieved up to 16% improvement and, for the overall CVS assessment, we achieved 5% improvement in balanced accuracy compared to DeepCVS under the same experiment settings. (Abstract)
behaviour: CVS criteria (C1-C3) and overall CVS assessment; balanced accuracy
setting: CVS6K: 6,000 frames from 100 Cholec80/m2cai16-workflow videos not used for development (same public source; no other centre)
contrast: none (method vs DeepCVS on the same evaluation set; no internal vs external comparison)
D1_quote: "The 100 videos which are not included in the semantic segmentation datasets are used to construct the CVS evaluation set." (Datasets section)
D2_quote: "The combined Cholec80 [31]and m2cai16-workflow [32] dataset consists of 117 videos after excluding duplicate cases [24]." (Datasets section)
D4_quote: "The evaluation set, named CVS6K, consists of 6,000 frames with only binary CVS annotations." (Datasets section; per-criterion positive/negative counts not found)
D5_quote: "we achieved 5% improvement in balanced accuracy compared to DeepCVS under the same experiment settings." (Abstract; Table III reports per-criterion balanced accuracy)
D6_quote: "For each frame, we assign three binary labels corresponding to the three criteria of CVS as suggested by SAGES [6]." ... "All annotations on the CVS evaluation dataset are verified independently by two experienced oncology surgeons (co-authors)." (Datasets section)

notes: Rated from arXiv v1 preprint, not the IEEE ICHI version of record (not retrieved). The abstract makes no external-generalisation claim; the review's 'external' label is not supported by the report: evaluation videos come from the same public datasets (Cholec80/m2cai16) as development data. claim_supported=yes refers to the stated comparative claim only. No development-set balanced accuracy reported. Verbatim quotes obtained through web text extraction extraction.

setting: (1) Davis16+EndoVis15 -> EndoVis17/EndoVis18 (porcine); (2) EndoVis17+18 -> HKPWH (4 x 100-frame prostatectomy sequences, Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong)
contrast: Across scenarios (larger vs smaller domain shift) and vs other methods; no source-domain performance
D1_quote: "HKPWH is a newly collected real-world surgical dataset from Hong Kong Prince of Wales Hospital." (Sec. 4.1 Datasets)
D2_quote: "the model is trained with largescale general videos and tested on the in-vivo surgical videos from EndoVis17 or EndoVis18 datasets." (Sec. 4.1, Experimental setup)
D4_quote: "It contains 4 × 100-frame fully annotated in-vivo sequences that record 4 surgery phases of prostatectomy" (Sec. 4.1)
D5_quote: "We employ the mean intersection-over-union (IoU) and Dice coefficient (Dice) to quantitatively analyze the results" (Sec. 4.2)
D6_quote: "We use the groundtruth masks from the binary task." (Sec. 4.1, EndoVis17)
D7_quote: "Base sets a higher baseline (57.2% IoU and 71.0% Dice) than that in Table 2 because of the smaller domain shift between public and in-house surgical videos." (Sec. 4.4)

supportable_claim: With the labelled first frame of each target video and online test-time adaptation, AOMA gave higher mean IoU than the compared methods on EndoVis17/18 (77.1/68.4; online-adaptation hyper-parameters and ablations chosen on these target sets) and on 4 HKPWH sequences of unreported patient number (80.1), with ~1.8 s adaptation time; the source-trained model without adaptation reached 60.5/47.2/57.2 IoU.
notes: Rule R1: claim covers both scenarios. D1: HKPWH from another hospital and human vs porcine EndoVis; scenario 1 general/ex-vivo source vs in-vivo porcine target; disjoint by dataset, not stated at patient level; number of HKPWH patients not reported. D2: HKPWH centre stated (m for scenario 2), EndoVis17/18 centre not stated (scenario 1), so p overall. D3: no code statement; HKPWH availability not stated; EndoVis public. D6: HKPWH annotators/protocol not described ('fully annotated'). D7 (R2): cross-scenario difference attributed to domain shift with no source-domain performance. D8 (R3): Base (K=0) is a clearly separated zero-shot estimate, but the claim rests on AOMA, which adapts on external labelled first frames by design, and gamma/sigma were selected and ablations run on EndoVis17/18 (target sets of scenario 1). Decision rules applied: (R1) a single claim sentence naming several external datasets/scenarios is rated across all of them and the lower rating is recorded; (R2) D7 is rated when the report presents development and external results for the model or interprets a cross-setting difference, x otherwise; (R3) D8 is rated even when D7 is x if the report documents changing the model or operating threshold on the external data; if a zero-shot estimate is clearly separated but the claim rests on the adapted/tuned estimate, D8 = p; (R4) data 'available on request' with no code or manifest = D3 a.
